metaData.originalTitle: 126 天后，扣子升级到 3.0：「@ 一下，全员就位」
metaData.title: 126 Days Later, Coze Upgrades to 3.0: 'Tag Everyone, All Hands on Deck'
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth review of Coze 3.0's core updates, including multi-Agent collaboration and local Agent integration, through a complete hands-on test of building a Shopify e-commerce Agent Team, showcasing the entire process from research to prototype implementation.
metaData.summary: From the perspective of the 'Crossroads' team, this article offers a deep hands-on review of the major Coze 3.0 update. Core updates include: the Agent Team multi-Agent collaboration system, local Agent integration (supporting Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw), and a project-based workflow overhaul. Using the construction of an e-commerce product selection Agent Team as a case study, the author breaks down the complete workflow: main Agent coordination, sub-Agent division of labor (Xiaohongshu research/overseas hot product research/product planning), and local Codex programming Agent implementation. The article particularly emphasizes the practical value of local Agent integration: users can connect their preferred tools (such as Codex) to the Coze platform, which then centrally manages and schedules them. This eliminates the need to build an Agent system from scratch, significantly reducing migration costs. The core advantage of multi-Agent division of labor is that each Agent can focus on its area of expertise, resulting in overall performance superior to a single general-purpose Agent.

mainPoints.point: Coze 3.0 Core Updates: Multi-Agent Collaboration System and Local Agent Integration.
mainPoints.explanation: Supports forming an Agent Team where a main Agent coordinates and dispatches sub-Agents to execute tasks in parallel. Also supports a one-line command to integrate local Agent CLIs (e.g., Codex), enabling the fusion and scheduling of cloud and local tools.

mainPoints.point: Multi-Agent Division of Labor Outperforms a Single General-Purpose Agent.
mainPoints.explanation: Each Agent focuses on its area of expertise (e.g., research, programming), achieving an overall score of around 85. In contrast, a single general-purpose Agent handling everything might only score 70 on each task, a gap that becomes evident in specific tasks.

mainPoints.point: Local Agent Integration Reduces Migration Costs and Preserves User Tool Preferences.
mainPoints.explanation: Users can directly connect their familiar local Agent tools (e.g., Codex) to the Coze platform, which manages and schedules them centrally. This eliminates the need to rebuild or switch windows, significantly lowering the barrier to entry.

keyQuotes: In Coze 3.0, you can assemble an entire Agent Team. Tag everyone, and all hands are on deck.
First, make the Agent capable of working. Then, equip the Agent with tools. Finally, have multiple Agents collaborate.
The most obvious value of multi-Agent division of labor is that every task finds a more suitable way to be handled.
Bring in the tools you're already using and manage them with Coze 3.0. There's no need to build an 'Agent system' from scratch.
Separately, each Agent can achieve around 85 points on its own task. But if you give everything to a single general-purpose Agent, each task might only get 70 points.

relatedArticles.title: 1.2k Stars in a Week, a Dark Horse Emerges in a Hot Track! Interview with Multica's Zhang Jiayuan: How to Rewrite the Rules of 'Human-AI Collaboration'?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article is an in-depth interview with Zhang Jiayuan, founder of the AI collaboration platform Multica, exploring how its kanban-style interface enables efficient 'multi-human + multi-agent' collaboration, and sharing the team's real-world experience using agents and their thoughts on AI-native organizational structures.

relatedArticles.title: “Is AGI Here? I Used It for a Week and My Scalp Tingled” | A Conversation with Zhang Haoran: Co-founder of Moxt
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through an in-depth interview with Moxt co-founder Zhang Haoran, this article explores how AI Native Workspaces are reshaping file systems and collaboration models to evolve organizations from 'human-computer interaction' to 'AI team collaboration.'

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: The Super Individual | To The Crazy Ones
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the essence of the 'Super Individual,' arguing it is not a result of skill training but a fundamental personality structure driven by curiosity, and suggests that large companies should inspire rather than cultivate such individuals by providing complete closed loops.

relatedArticles.title: Mastering OpenClaw: Core Architecture, Working Principles, and Agent Deployment Steps
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core architecture, memory management mechanisms, and multi-agent collaboration principles of the AI Agent framework OpenClaw, along with detailed hardware deployment suggestions and practical use cases.

relatedArticles.title: MiniMax M2.7: Unlocking Model Self-Evolution
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: MiniMax releases the M2.7 model, featuring 'model self-evolution' capabilities and achieving significant breakthroughs in software engineering, professional office productivity, and multi-agent collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: 2026: The End of Software, the Fall of Engineers, the Disappearance of Mediocrity
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Using the sharp decline in US software stocks in early 2026 as a starting point, this article deeply analyzes how AI Agents are eroding the SaaS middle-layer business model, and explores structural shifts in software form from product to medium, and the engineer's role from writing code to understanding systems.

relatedArticles.title: What Are We Really Discussing When We Talk About Harness? | In-Depth Dialogue: MiniMax × Hermes Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article compiles an in-depth dialogue hosted by Crossroads, featuring the MiniMax Agent team and the head of Hermes Agent. It delves into the core topics surrounding the shift in hype from OpenClaw to Hermes, exploring the definitions of Agent and Harness, multi-agent collaboration, self-evolution, the gap between Chinese and US models, and entrepreneurial opportunities in Agent Infra.

relatedArticles.title: One AI Is Not Enough
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: MiniMax introduces Mavis, a multi-agent collaboration system that uses a Leader-Worker-Verifier architecture and adversarial quality gates to solve the pain points of single agents in complex tasks, sharing its design philosophy, technical architecture, cost considerations, and applicable scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: The Era of Super Individuals | Tencent Research Institute's 30,000-Word Report
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on field research and experiments, the Tencent Research Institute proposes that the core driving force of organizational change in the AI era is bottom-up emergence, with the central proposition being 'How do super individuals aggregate into super teams,' and systematically elaborates on the birth, aggregation paths, team forms, and operational mechanisms of super individuals.
